title: A coherent module whose support is a union of two closed subsets is an extension of modules supported on each
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=\{x\in X:\mathcal G_x\ne0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](2), $\mathcal G_x$ the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Suppose $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=Z\cup Z'$ with $Z,Z'\subseteq X$ closed subsets. Then there is a coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal F$ such that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G')\subseteq Z'$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F/\mathcal G')\subseteq Z$, where $\mathcal F/\mathcal G'$ is the cokernel of the inclusion $\mathcal G'\to\mathcal F$ (a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module); that is, a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to0$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G'\subseteq Z'$ and $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G\subseteq Z$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YD (label lemma-prepare-filter-support, coherent.tex line 2944), proof lines 2956-2979 (uses Schemes Lemma 01J3 schemes-lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme and Lemma 01Y9 lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf on the Noetherian open X minus Z'). Tags verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags: 01YD,coherent-lemma-prepare-filter-support; 01J3; 01Y9

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal I=\mathcal I_Z\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be the sheaf of ideals of the reduced induced closed subscheme structure on the closed subset $Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] (1): it is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and on every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$ one has $\mathcal I(U)=I$, the radical ideal with $V(I)=Z\cap U$. Put $V(\mathcal I)=\{x\in X:\mathcal I_x
eq\mathcal O_{X,x}\}$, the stalk $\mathcal I_x$ being an ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine]. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine], $V(\mathcal I)\cap U=V(\mathcal I(U))=V(I)=Z\cap U$ for every affine open $U$; affine opens cover $X$, so $V(\mathcal I)=Z$. In particular $\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for every $x
otin Z$, and $\mathcal I_x
eq\mathcal O_{X,x}$ for every $x\in Z$.

proof.text: For $n\ge1$ let $\mathcal I^n$ and $\mathcal G'_n=\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0), and $\mathcal G_n=\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ the cokernel of the inclusion $\iota_n:\mathcal G'_n\to\mathcal F$; for $n=0$ put $\mathcal G'_0=\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G_0=\mathcal F/\mathcal F=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1) (applied inductively with $\mathcal J=\mathcal I$ and the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal I^{n-1}$, resp. $\mathcal F$: each $\mathcal I^n$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, $\mathcal F$ being coherent hence quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]) $\mathcal G'_n$ is a quasi-coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module of the coherent module $\mathcal F$; since $X$ is locally Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] (2) shows that $\mathcal G'_n$ and $\mathcal G_n$ are coherent.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YD (lemma-prepare-filter-support), proof, coherent.tex lines 2956-2979: 'Consider the subsheaves $\mathcal G'_n=\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ and the quotients $\mathcal G_n=\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$' (coherence: section intro, 'a quasi-coherent subquotient of a coherent sheaf is coherent')

proof.text: For each $n$ the sequence $0\to\mathcal G'_n\xrightarrow{\iota_n}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{c_n}\mathcal G_n\to0$, $c_n$ the cokernel map, is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5) it suffices to check exactness on stalks at every $x\in X$: $(\iota_n)_x$ is injective by (1) of that lemma ($\iota_n$ is injective on sections), $(c_n)_x$ is surjective with kernel $(\iota_n)_x((\mathcal G'_n)_x)$ by (3), and $c_n\circ\iota_n=0$. (For $n=0$ the sequence is $0\to\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal F\to0\to0$.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YD (lemma-prepare-filter-support), proof, coherent.tex lines 2956-2979: 'For each $n$ we have a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal G'_n\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G_n\to0$'

proof.text: $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G_n)\subseteq Z$ for every $n$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] (2). For $n=0$, $\mathcal G_0=0$. For $n\ge1$ and $x\notin Z$, step 1 gives $\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, so $(\mathcal I_x)^n=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and, by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk] (4), $(\mathcal G_n)_x\cong\mathcal F_x/(\mathcal I_x)^n\mathcal F_x=\mathcal F_x/\mathcal F_x=0$. (The source states this for $x\in Z'\setminus Z$; the argument holds for every $x\notin Z$.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YD (lemma-prepare-filter-support), proof, coherent.tex lines 2956-2979: 'For every point $x$ of $Z'\setminus Z$ we have $\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and hence $\mathcal G_{n,x}=0$. Thus we see that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G_n)\subset Z$'

proof.text: Let $V=X\setminus Z'$, an open subset; the open subscheme $V$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The restriction $\mathcal F|_V$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_V$-module [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover] (1), and $\mathcal I|_V\subseteq\mathcal O_V$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (2). For $x\in V$ the open neighbourhoods of $x$ contained in $V$ are cofinal among all open neighbourhoods of $x$, so by the definition of stalks as colimits [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] $(\mathcal F|_V)_x=\mathcal F_x$, $(\mathcal I|_V)_x=\mathcal I_x$ and $\mathcal O_{V,x}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F|_V)=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\cap V=(Z\cup Z')\setminus Z'\subseteq Z$, and for $x\in Z\cap V$ step 1 gives $(\mathcal I|_V)_x=\mathcal I_x\neq\mathcal O_{X,x}=\mathcal O_{V,x}$; thus $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F|_V)\subseteq V(\mathcal I|_V)=\{x\in V:(\mathcal I|_V)_x\neq\mathcal O_{V,x}\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-support-power-ideal-kills] applied to the Noetherian scheme $V$, the coherent module $\mathcal F|_V$ and the ideal $\mathcal K=\mathcal I|_V$, there is $t\ge0$ with $(\mathcal I|_V)^t(\mathcal F|_V)=0$ (with $(\mathcal I|_V)^0(\mathcal F|_V)=\mathcal F|_V$).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YD (lemma-prepare-filter-support), proof, coherent.tex lines 2956-2979: 'Note that $X\setminus Z'$ is a Noetherian scheme. Hence by Lemma 01Y9 there exists an $n$ such that $\mathcal G'_n|_{X\setminus Z'}=\mathcal I^n\mathcal F|_{X\setminus Z'}=0$'

proof.text: $(\mathcal I^t\mathcal F)|_V=(\mathcal I|_V)^t(\mathcal F|_V)$ as submodules of $\mathcal F|_V$: for $t=0$ both are $\mathcal F|_V$; for $t\ge1$, [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (3) gives $(\mathcal J\mathcal G)|_V=(\mathcal J|_V)(\mathcal G|_V)$ for every quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J$ and quasi-coherent $\mathcal G$, which applied with $\mathcal G=\mathcal I^{k}$ gives $(\mathcal I^{k+1})|_V=(\mathcal I|_V)^{k+1}$ by induction on $k$, and then with $\mathcal J=\mathcal I^t$, $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$ gives the claim. Hence $\mathcal G'_t|_V=0$ by step 5, so $(\mathcal G'_t)_x=(\mathcal G'_t|_V)_x=0$ for every $x\in V$ (stalks as in step 5) and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G'_t)\subseteq X\setminus V=Z'$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YD (lemma-prepare-filter-support), proof, coherent.tex lines 2956-2979: 'For such an $n$ we see that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G'_n)\subset Z'$'

proof.text: Put $\mathcal G'=\mathcal G'_t$ and $\mathcal G=\mathcal G_t$: by steps 2-6, $0\to\mathcal G'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to0$ is a short exact sequence of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal F$ a coherent submodule, $\mathcal G=\mathcal F/\mathcal G'$, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G')\subseteq Z'$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)\subseteq Z$.
